verdict:
NO ENTRY - but escalate, because the record that produced this verdict had a sign error on net cash and a basis error on gross margin, and the bench that found them is the one with LOWER conviction.

START WITH WHAT THE MARKET SOLD AND WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED. The priced narrative was that neffy's payer access stalled and the burn is unfinanceable. The demand half of that is refuted outright: US net product revenue went $12.8M to $17.5M to $26.2M across the last three quarters - plus 50% sequentially, plus 105% year over year - total US epinephrine share doubled from 2.5% to 5%, share in targeted accounts went 4% to 8%, and unique prescribers roughly tripled to more than 16,000. And the company achieved that with ZERO new commercial formulary additions in the July 1 cycle. That is a launch working through prescriber pull rather than coverage, which is harder and more durable than the reverse. The stock fell 7.4% into that print. Something else is being priced.

THE SOMETHING ELSE IS THE FINANCING - AND BOTH THE TRIAGE AND RED GOT ITS MAGNITUDE WRONG BY A SIGN. Every prior document in this file carried net cash at roughly minus $28M: $143.8M of cash less a $96.7M term loan less a $74.9M 'ALK financing liability.' Blue pulled the financing-liability note and the third item is not debt. It arose from $145M of upfront plus $10M of milestones ARS has ALREADY RECEIVED for the EEA license. It has no maturity. It has no cash-repayment mechanism. It GROWS as ALK books sales-based royalties. It is extinguished only if ARS voluntarily exercises a repurchase option. This is failed-sale accounting - the cash came in, the revenue could not be recognized, so the receipt sits on the balance sheet looking exactly like borrowing. Corrected net cash is approximately PLUS $47M. Blue is right, and this is the single best piece of analysis in the batch. A single-product launcher growing 105% year over year with positive net cash is a categorically different downside than the negative-net-cash story red prosecuted.

THEN RED PROSECUTED A BASIS ARTIFACT USING A BASIS ARTIFACT. Red's FATAL was that the '62% gross margin' in the record is fake. Red is right that it is fake - I credit the catch - the 62% is gross profit over TOTAL revenue including $7.4M of zero-COGS-attributed partner revenue, and it appears in neither the press release nor the 10-Q, which makes it a genuine venue-absence finding. But red's replacement figure commits the identical error in the opposite direction: it divides TOTAL COGS of $12.85M by PRODUCT-ONLY revenue of $26.21M to get 51%. The $7.391M is SUPPLY revenue - neffy physically shipped to ALK, Alfresa, Pediatrix and Seqirus at transfer price - and the 10-Q confirms COGS includes the manufacturing cost of that supplied product with no product-versus-supply split disclosed. Numerator and denominator do not match. The honest answer is that product margin is bounded between 51% and about 78% and is NOT DISCLOSED. The triage's original label - unresolved - was correct all along, and red converted an open question into a FATAL by picking the worst corner of the interval. Red's 'needs 4x product revenue to break even' is that worst corner, not the estimate.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS ENOUGH TO STAY OUT. The timing legs, all of which blue strengthened rather than softened. Cash fell $101.2M in the first half. Second-half cash operating expense is guided at $100-110M. The corrected bridge puts year-end 2026 at roughly $81-94M and mid-2027 at roughly $25-55M before debt service, against a $96.7M term loan whose covenants NOBODY HAS READ - the Credit Agreement exhibit sits in the July 8-Ks and neither bench pulled it. A raise in the first half of 2027 is PROBABLE, not arithmetically forced, and blue is right to make that correction too. Meanwhile blue found the shelf: an S-3ASR automatic shelf, unlimited, filed January 2025 - so the mechanics to raise are already in place and can be used on a day's notice. There are no new formulary adds available until the January 2027 cycle. And there is a securities class action with a class period of March 9 to June 24 2026 over CVS Caremark coverage statements, with a lead-plaintiff deadline of October 5 2026.

THE ENTRY EVENT IS THE RAISE PRICING, NOT THE PRINT. Buying a probable dilutive financing from the wrong side is donating the better entry, and the zero-cost inventory that is currently flattering COGS ($6.7M down to $3.1M held) will be substantially exhausted by then, which means the Q3 or Q4 print also resolves the margin interval. Wait for both. This is a genuine WATCH with dated triggers, not red's 'nothing to own' - and the distinction matters because red's version would have taken the name off the board entirely on two numbers that were wrong.

ONE ITEM NEITHER BENCH RESOLVED AND I AM NOT RESOLVING EITHER. Blue flagged that the 10-Q legal note reads 'no material pending legal proceedings' while a securities class action was live. That is only a real inconsistency if the complaint was filed before the 10-Q was filed on 8/13. The class period closes 6/24/26 and the Robbins reminder release is mid-August, so the filing sequence is genuinely ambiguous from the documents in hand. The test is one docket lookup: complaint filing date versus 2026-08-13. If the complaint predates the filing, this is a disclosure-integrity finding on a name whose entire class action is ABOUT disclosure integrity, which would be material to more than sizing. Do not let this sit as a footnote.
blue_ruling: PARTIALLY OVERTURNED, and on the two numbers that carried the case. Blue OVERTURNED red's finding that the ALK financing liability is a fixed obligation - flipping net cash from minus $28M to plus $47M, a sign change on the decisive balance-sheet figure that the triage AND red had both carried - and REDUCED red's FATAL margin finding from 'resolved bearishly' to NOT_DISCLOSED with product margin bounded between 51% and roughly 78%. Both benches still land on no entry, but they land there for different reasons, and red's reasons were wrong.
reopen_gates: EVENT (this is THE entry event): the equity raise PRICING. A live S-3ASR means it can be executed overnight. Buying ahead of a probable dilutive financing gives up the better entry for no compensation; buying the printed deal is the trade.

DATA: Q3 disclosure that splits product COGS from supply COGS, or product-only gross margin disclosed directly, with the zero-cost pre-approval inventory substantially exhausted ($6.7M down to $3.1M held at 6/30 - it is nearly gone). This collapses the [51%, ~78%] interval and is the single number that decides whether breakeven needs 2.5x or 4x. It is the highest-value disclosure on the calendar for this name.

DATA (must be closed before ANY sizing, and it is a plain document pull, not a research project): the Credit Agreement covenant text from the 2026-07-07 and 2026-07-17 8-Ks, accessions 0001193125-26-297554 and 0001193125-26-307773. A minimum-liquidity covenant on the $96.7M term loan would convert a probable 1H27 raise into a forced one. Neither bench read it and both said so.
EVENT: a non-dilutive financing 8-K - ex-US royalty monetization or further ALK monetization - covering the 1H27 gap. Note this hatch is already half-spent: $155M of EEA economics has been received.
EVENT: formulary adds in the January 2027 cycle. This is the next available coverage catalyst; there is none before it.

LEGAL: securities class action lead-plaintiff deadline 2026-10-05, class period 2026-03-09 to 2026-06-24 over CVS Caremark coverage statements. Resolve the complaint filing date against the 10-Q filing date of 2026-08-13 first - see the verdict text.
